sanskrit: yudhyatām eva teṣāṃ tu tadā vānararakṣasām ravir astaṃ gato rātriḥ pravṛttā prāṇahāriṇī
english: While those monkeys and rākṣasas were still fighting, the sun set and night came on — a night that robs creatures of their lives.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ baddhavairāṇāṃ ghorāṇāṃ jayam icchatām saṃpravṛttaṃ niśāyuddhaṃ tadā vāraṇarakṣasām
english: A night battle then broke out between those monkeys and rākṣasas — terrible foes bound together in mutual hatred, each craving victory.

sanskrit: rākṣaso 'sīti harayo hariś cāsīti rākṣasāḥ anyonyaṃ samare jaghnus tasmiṃs tamasi dāruṇe
english: "You are a rākṣasa!" cried the monkeys; "You are a monkey!" cried the rākṣasas — and so they slew one another in that dreadful darkness.

sanskrit: jahi dāraya caitīti kathaṃ vidravasīti ca evaṃ sutumulaḥ śabdas tasmiṃs tamasi śuśruve
english: "Strike! Tear him apart!" — "Why do you flee?" — such a tremendous clamour was heard throughout that darkness.

sanskrit: kālāḥ kāñcanasaṃnāhās tasmiṃs tamasi rākṣasāḥ saṃprādṛśyanta śailendrā dīptauṣadhivanā iva
english: Dark-complexioned rākṣasas clad in golden armour appeared in that darkness like mountain kings whose slopes blaze with luminous herbs.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tamasi duṣpāre rākṣasāḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ paripetur mahāvegā bhakṣayantaḥ plavaṃgamān
english: In that impenetrable darkness, rākṣasas maddened by rage charged with great speed, devouring the monkeys.

sanskrit: te hayān kāñcanāpīḍan dhvajāṃś cāgniśikhopamān āplutya daśanais tīkṣṇair bhīmakopā vyadārayan
english: Leaping upon horses adorned with golden crests and banners resembling tongues of fire, those rākṣasas, furious with terrible wrath, tore them apart with their sharp fangs.

sanskrit: kuñjarān kuñjarārohān patākādhvajino rathān cakarṣuś ca dadaṃśuś ca daśanaiḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ
english: Maddened with rage, they dragged and bit with their teeth at elephants, elephant riders, chariots flying banners and standards.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi rāmaś ca śarair āśīviṣomapaiḥ dṛśyādṛśyāni rakṣāṃsi pravarāṇi nijaghnatuḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, with arrows equal to venomous serpents, struck down the choicest rākṣasas whether visible or invisible.

sanskrit: turaṃgakhuravidhvastaṃ rathanemisamuddhatam rurodha karṇanetrāṇiṇyudhyatāṃ dharaṇīrajaḥ
english: The dust of the earth, churned up by the hooves of horses and thrown up by the rims of chariot wheels, choked the ears and eyes of the combatants.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā ghore saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe rudhirodā mahāvegā nadyas tatra prasusruvuḥ
english: While that dreadful, hair-raising battle raged, rivers of blood flowed swiftly there.

sanskrit: tato bherīmṛdaṅgānāṃ paṇavānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ śaṅkhaveṇusvanonmiśraḥ saṃbabhūvādbhutopamaḥ
english: Then arose a din of kettle-drums, battle-drums, and paṇava drums, mingled with the sounds of conches and flutes — a sound beyond wonder.

sanskrit: hatānāṃ stanamānānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca nisvanaḥ śastrāṇāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca saṃbabhūvātidāruṇaḥ
english: The cries of rākṣasas who had been struck down and were groaning, and the clash of the monkeys' weapons, together raised an exceedingly dreadful sound.

sanskrit: śastrapuṣpopahārā ca tatrāsīd yuddhamedinī durjñeyā durniveśā ca śoṇitāsravakardamā
english: The battlefield was strewn with an offering of weapons as flowers; it was hard to traverse, hard to enter, a quagmire of streaming blood.

sanskrit: sā babhūva niśā ghorā harirākṣasahāriṇī kālarātrīva bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ duratikramā
english: That night was dreadful, sweeping away monkeys and rākṣasas alike — like the Night of Doom for all living beings, impossible to cross over.

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasās tatra tasmiṃs tamasi dāruṇe rāmam evābhyadhāvanta saṃhṛṣṭā śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then in that dreadful darkness, the rākṣasas, filled with joy, charged straight at Rāma alone, raining arrows upon him.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śabdaḥ kruddhānām abhigarjatām udvarta iva saptānāṃ samudrāṇām abhūt svanaḥ
english: The roar of those raging rākṣasas rushing forward was like the surging tumult of seven oceans.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ rāmaḥ śaraiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaḍ jaghāna niśācarān nimeṣāntaramātreṇa śitair agniśikhopamaiḥ
english: Rāma felled six of those night-roamers with six sharp arrows keen as flames of fire — in the mere twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: yajñaśatruś ca durdharṣo mahāpārśvamahodarau vajradaṃṣṭro mahākāyas tau cobhau śukasāraṇau
english: Yajñaśatru the irresistible, Mahāpārśva, Mahodara, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Mahākāya, and those two, Śuka and Sāraṇa —

sanskrit: te tu rāmeṇa bāṇaughaḥ sarvamarmasu tāḍitāḥ yuddhād apasṛtās tatra sāvaśeṣāyuṣo 'bhavan
english: — these were struck by Rāma's flood of arrows at every vital point, and withdrawing from the battle they survived with their remaining span of life.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgaiḥ śarair agniśikhopamaiḥ diśaś cakāra vimalāḥ pradiśaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Then the mighty Rāma, with arrows of golden-variegated shafts resembling tongues of fire, made the cardinal and intermediate directions clear.

sanskrit: ye tv anye rākṣasā vīrā rāmasyābhimukhe sthitāḥ te 'pi naṣṭāḥ samāsādya pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: Whatever other warrior rākṣasas stood facing Rāma also perished upon approaching him, like moths meeting a flame.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair viśikhaiḥ saṃpatadbhiḥ sahasraśaḥ babhūva rajanī citrā khadyotair iva śāradī
english: With thousands of shafts tipped with gold flying through the air, the night became brilliant, like an autumnal night lit with fireflies.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ ca ninadair harīṇāṃ cāpi garjitaiḥ sā babhūva niśā ghorā bhūyo ghoratarā tadā
english: With the roaring of the rākṣasas and the battle-cries of the monkeys, that already dreadful night became even more dreadful.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā pravṛddhena samantataḥ trikūṭaḥ kandarākīrṇaḥ pravyāharad ivācalaḥ
english: By that great swelling sound on all sides, Mount Trikūṭa, filled with its caverns, seemed to roar back in echo.

sanskrit: golāṅgūlā mahākāyās tamasā tulyavarcasaḥ saṃpariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ bhakṣayan rajanīcarān
english: Golāṅgūla monkeys of massive bodies, matching the darkness in their dark hue, seized night-roaming rākṣasas in their arms and devoured them.

sanskrit: aṅgadas tu raṇe śatruṃ nihantuṃ samupasthitaḥ rāvaṇer nijaghānāśu sārathiṃ ca hayān api
english: Aṅgada, pressing forward in battle to slay the enemy, swiftly struck down Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit's charioteer and his horses.

sanskrit: indrajit tu rathaṃ tyaktvā hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ aṅgadena mahāmāyas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: But Indrajit, master of great illusion, his horses slain and his charioteer killed, abandoned his chariot and vanished right there before Aṅgada.

sanskrit: so 'ntardhāna gataḥ pāpo rāvaṇī raṇakarkaśaḥ brahmadattavaro vīro rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ adṛśyo niśitān bāṇān mumocāśanivarcasaḥ
english: That wicked one, Rāvaṇa's son, fierce in battle, having vanished from sight — the heroic Rāvaṇi, empowered by the boon of Brahmā, maddened by rage — released sharp arrows blazing like thunderbolts while invisible.

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva ghorair nāgamayaiḥ śaraiḥ bibheda samare kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rākṣasaḥ
english: That rākṣasa, enraged, pierced both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa throughout all their limbs in battle with dreadful arrows made of nāgas.

sanskrit: sa tasya gatim anvicchan rājaputraḥ pratāpavān dideśātibalo rāmo daśavānarayūthapān
english: The valiant prince Rāma, immensely powerful, seeking to track Indrajit's movements, dispatched ten monkey chieftains.

sanskrit: dvau suṣeṇasya dāyādau nīlaṃ ca plavagarṣabham aṅgadaṃ vāliputraṃ ca śarabhaṃ ca tarasvinam
english: The two sons of Suṣeṇa, Nīla the foremost among monkeys, Aṅgada the son of Vālin, and swift Śarabha —

sanskrit: vinataṃ jāmbavantaṃ ca sānuprasthaṃ mahābalam ṛṣabhaṃ carṣabhaskandham ādideśa paraṃtapaḥ
english: — Vinata, Jāmbavān, the mighty Sānuprastha, Ṛṣabha, and Ṛṣabhaskandha — these the scorcher of foes commanded.

sanskrit: te saṃprahṛṣṭā harayo bhīmān udyamya pādapān ākāśaṃ viviśuḥ sarve mārgāmāṇā diśo daśa
english: Those monkeys, greatly excited, lifting terrible trees, all leapt into the sky and searched the ten directions.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vegavatāṃ vegam iṣubhir vegavattaraiḥ astravit paramāstreṇa vārayām āsa rāvaṇiḥ
english: The son of Rāvaṇa, skilled in the science of missiles, checked the speed of those swift warriors with arrows even swifter, using his supreme weapon.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmavegā harayo nārācaiḥ kṣatavikṣatāḥ andhakāre na dadṛśur meghaiḥ sūryam ivāvṛtam
english: The monkeys of fearsome speed, wounded and struck by iron arrows, could not see him in the darkness — as one cannot see the sun covered by clouds.

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇayor eva sarvamarmabhidaḥ śarān bhṛśam āveśayām āsa rāvaṇiḥ samitiṃjayaḥ
english: Rāvaṇi, ever victorious in battle, drove deeply into Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa alone arrows that pierced every vital point.

sanskrit: nirantaraśarīrau tu bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau kruddhenendrajitā vīrau pannagaiḥ śaratāṃ gataiḥ
english: The two heroic brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, their bodies covered without interval, were struck by the enraged Indrajit with serpent-arrows — arrows that had become serpents.

sanskrit: tayoḥ kṣatajamārgeṇa susrāva rudhiraṃ bahu tāv ubhau ca prakāśete puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Blood flowed copiously through the wound-paths on both of them; those two shone like kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: tataḥ paryantaraktākṣo bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ rāvaṇir bhrātarau vākyam antardhānagato 'bravīt
english: Then Rāvaṇi, his eyes reddened at the corners, resembling a heap of broken collyrium, invisible, spoke these words to the two brothers.

sanskrit: yudhyamānam anālakṣyaṃ śakro 'pi tridaśeśvaraḥ draṣṭum āsādituṃ vāpi na śaktaḥ kiṃ punar yuvām
english: "Even Śakra, lord of the thirty gods, is incapable of seeing or approaching me when I fight invisibly — how much less you two?"

sanskrit: prāvṛtāv iṣujālena rāghavau kaṅkapatriṇā eṣa roṣaparītātmā nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "I shall now, my soul seized with fury, send both Rāghava brothers — enveloped in a net of heron-feathered arrows — to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu dharmajñau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau nirbibheda śitair bāṇaiḥ prajaharṣa nanāda ca
english: Having spoken thus, he pierced the two brothers — Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, knowers of dharma — with sharp arrows, and exulted and roared.

sanskrit: bhinnāñjanacayaśyāmo visphārya vipulaṃ dhanuḥ bhūyo bhūyaḥ śarān ghorān visasarja mahāmṛdhe
english: Dark as a heap of shattered collyrium, he drew his great bow and released dreadful arrows again and again in that great battle.

sanskrit: tato marmasu marmajño majjayan niśitāñ śarān rāmalakṣmaṇayor vīro nanāda ca muhur muhuḥ
english: Then that heroic knower of vital points, driving sharp arrows into the vital points of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, roared again and again.

sanskrit: baddhau tu śarabandhena tāv ubhau raṇamūrdhani nimeṣāntaramātreṇa na śekatur udīkṣitum
english: Those two, bound by the bond of arrows at the forefront of battle, could not even look up for the mere twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: tato vibhinnasarvāṅgau śaraśalyācitāv ubhau dhvajāv iva mahendrasya rajjumuktau prakampitau
english: Then both of them, their every limb pierced, covered with arrow-thorns, swayed like the banner of great Indra released from its ropes.

sanskrit: tau saṃpracalitau vīrau marmabhedena karśitau nipetatur maheṣvāsau jagatyāṃ jagatīpatī
english: Those two heroes, those two great bowmen, lords of the earth, staggering and weakened by the piercing of their vital points, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tau vīraśayane vīrau śayānau rudhirokṣitau śaraveṣṭitasarvāṅgāv ārtau paramapīḍitau
english: Those two heroes lay on their hero's bed, drenched in blood, their every limb wrapped in arrows, agonized and in extreme pain.

sanskrit: na hy aviddhaṃ tayor gātraṃ babhūvāṅgulam antaram nānirbhinnaṃ na cāstabdham ā karāgrād ajihmagaiḥ
english: Not a finger's breadth of their bodies was unpierced; not a part was not split, not a part was not transfixed from fingertip to the rest, by those straight-flying arrows.

sanskrit: tau tu krūreṇa nihatau rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā asṛksusruvatus tīvraṃ jalaṃ prasravaṇāv iva
english: Struck down by that cruel shape-shifting rākṣasa, the two of them bled profusely, like a pair of mountain springs flowing with water.

sanskrit: papāta prathamaṃ rāmo viddho marmasu mārgaṇaiḥ krodhād indrajitā yena purā śakro vinirjitaḥ
english: Rāma fell first, pierced in his vital points by the arrows of Indrajit who in his wrath had previously vanquished Śakra himself.

sanskrit: nāracair ardhanārācair bhallair añjalikair api vivyādha vatsadantaiś ca siṃhadaṃṣṭraiḥ kṣurais tathā
english: He shot him with nārāca arrows, ardha-nārāca arrows, bhalla arrows, añjalika arrows, vatsadanta arrows, siṃhadaṃṣṭra arrows, and kṣura arrows.

sanskrit: sa vīraśayane śiśye vijyam ādāya kārmukam bhinnamuṣṭiparīṇāhaṃ triṇataṃ rukmabhūṣitam
english: He lay on his warrior's bed, still holding his unstrung bow — its grip broken, triple-bent, ornamented with gold.

sanskrit: bāṇapātāntare rāmaṃ patitaṃ puruṣarṣabham sa tatra lakṣmaṇo dṛṣṭvā nirāśo jīvite 'bhavat
english: Seeing Rāma, that bull among men, fallen in the interval between the arrow-showers, Lakṣmaṇa lost all hope of life.

sanskrit: baddhau tu vīrau patitau śayānau tau vānarāḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ samāgatā vāyusutapramukhyā viṣadam ārtāḥ paramaṃ ca jagmuḥ
english: The two heroes, bound and fallen and lying there — the assembled monkeys, led by the son of the Wind, surrounded them and stood in utter sorrow, overwhelmed with the greatest grief.

sanskrit: tato dyāṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva vīkṣamāṇā vanaukasaḥ dadṛśuḥ saṃtatau bāṇair bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Then the forest dwellers, looking over sky and earth, saw the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa sewn together by arrows.

sanskrit: vṛṣṭvevoparate deve kṛtakarmaṇi rākṣase ājagāmātha taṃ deśaṃ sasugrīvo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: When the rākṣasa had completed his deed and ceased — as a cloud ceases after raining — Sugrīva arrived at that place together with Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: nīladvividamaindāś ca suṣeṇasumukhāṅgadāḥ tūrṇaṃ hanumatā sārdham anvaśocanta rāghavau
english: Nīla, Dvivida, Mainda, Suṣeṇa, Sumukha, and Aṅgada quickly lamented for the two Rāghava princes together with Hanumān.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭau mandaniḥśvāsau śoṇitaughapariplutau śarajālācitau stabdhau śayānau śaratalpayoḥ
english: Motionless, breathing faintly, drenched in floods of blood, covered with a mesh of arrows, rigid — they lay on their arrow-beds.

sanskrit: niḥśvasantau yathā sarpau niśceṣṭau mandavikramau rudhirasrāvadigdhāṅgau tāpanīyāv iva dhvajau
english: Hissing like serpents, motionless, their movement sluggish, their limbs smeared with flowing blood — they were like golden banners.

sanskrit: tau vīraśayane vīrau śayānau mandaceṣṭitau yūthapais taiḥ parivṛtau bāṣpavyākulalocanaiḥ
english: Those two heroes lay on the hero's bed, barely stirring, surrounded by monkey chieftains whose eyes were clouded with tears.

sanskrit: rāghavau patitau dṛṣṭvā śarajālasamāvṛtau babhūvur vyathitāḥ sarve vānarāḥ savibhīṣaṇāḥ
english: Seeing the two Rāghava princes fallen and enveloped in a net of arrows, all the monkeys along with Vibhīṣaṇa were stricken with anguish.

sanskrit: antarikṣaṃ nirīkṣanto diśaḥ sarvāś ca vānarāḥ na cainaṃ māyayā channaṃ dadṛśū rāvaṇiṃ raṇe
english: The monkeys scanned the sky and all directions but could not see Rāvaṇi in battle, veiled as he was by his māyā.

sanskrit: taṃ tu māyāpraticchinnaṃ māyayaiva vibhīṣaṇaḥ vīkṣamāṇo dadarśātha bhrātuḥ putram avasthitam
english: But Vibhīṣaṇa, looking through māyā with māyā, beheld his brother's son stationed there, though concealed by illusion.

sanskrit: tam apratima karmāṇam apratidvandvam āhave dadarśāntarhitaṃ vīraṃ varadānād vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: By virtue of his boon, Vibhīṣaṇa saw that hero of incomparable deeds, unrivalled in combat, hidden from sight.

sanskrit: indrajit tv ātmanaḥ karma tau śayānau samīkṣya ca uvāca paramaprīto harṣayan sarvanairṛtān
english: Indrajit, surveying his own deed and those two lying there, spoke in supreme delight, gladdening all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dūṣaṇasya ca hantārau kharasya ca mahābalau sāditau māmakair bāṇair bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "The two mighty brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — slayers of Dūṣaṇa and Khara — have been laid low by my arrows."

sanskrit: nemau mokṣayituṃ śakyāv etasmād iṣubandhanāt sarvair api samāgamya sarṣisaṅghaiḥ surāsuraiḥ
english: "These two cannot be freed from this bond of arrows even by all the gods, asuras, and hosts of sages combined."

sanskrit: yatkṛte cintayānasya śokārtasya pitur mama aspṛṣṭvā śayanaṃ gātrais triyāmā yāti śarvatī
english: "Because of these two, my father, brooding in grief, has been passing the night without his body touching his bed."

sanskrit: kṛtsneyaṃ yatkṛte laṅkā nadī varṣāsv ivākulā so 'yaṃ mūlaharo 'narthaḥ sarveṣāṃ nihato mayā
english: "Because of these two, all Laṅkā has been troubled like a river in the rains. That root-destroying calamity for all of us has been slain by me."

sanskrit: rāmasya lakṣmaṇasyaiva sarveṣāṃ ca vanaukasām vikramā niṣphalāḥ sarve yathā śaradi toyadāḥ
english: "All the exploits of Rāma, of Lakṣmaṇa, and of all the forest dwellers are now fruitless — like autumn clouds without rain."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu tān sarvān rākṣasān paripārśvagān yūthapān api tān sarvāṃs tāḍayām āsa rāvaṇiḥ
english: Having spoken thus to all those rākṣasas standing around him, Rāvaṇi also struck all those monkey chieftains.

sanskrit: tān ardayitvā bāṇaughais trāsayitvā ca vānarān prajahāsa mahābāhur vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Having tormented them with floods of arrows and frightened the monkeys, the long-armed one laughed aloud and spoke this further word.

sanskrit: śarabandhena ghoreṇa mayā baddhau camūmukhe sahitau bhrātarāv etau niśāmayata rākṣasāḥ
english: "Behold, rākṣasas! These two brothers together have been bound by me at the forefront of the army with a dreadful bond of arrows."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te sarve rākṣasāḥ kūṭayodhinaḥ paraṃ vismayam ājagmuḥ karmaṇā tena toṣitāḥ
english: Thus addressed, all those rākṣasa fighters by cunning were filled with the greatest amazement and satisfied by that feat.

sanskrit: vineduś ca mahānādān sarve te jaladopamāḥ hato rāma iti jñātvā rāvaṇiṃ samapūjayan
english: All those cloud-like rākṣasas roared great roars, and knowing Rāma to be slain, honoured Rāvaṇi.

sanskrit: niṣpandau tu tadā dṛṣṭvā tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau vasudhāyāṃ nirucchvāsau hatāv ity anvamanyata
english: Seeing both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa motionless on the ground, barely breathing, he deemed them slain.

sanskrit: harṣeṇa tu samāviṣṭa indrajit samitiṃjayaḥ praviveśa purīṃ laṅkāṃ harṣayan sarvanairṛtān
english: Filled with joy, Indrajit ever victorious in battle entered the city of Laṅkā, gladdening all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇayor dṛṣṭvā śarīre sāyakaiś cite sarvāṇi cāṅgopāṅgāni sugrīvaṃ bhayam āviśat
english: Seeing the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, their every limb and sub-limb heaped with shafts, fear overtook Sugrīva.

sanskrit: tam uvāca paritrastaṃ vānarendraṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ sabāṣpavadanaṃ dīnaṃ śokavyākulalocanam
english: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke to that terrified king of monkeys, whose face was wet with tears, who was dejected, his eyes bewildered with grief.

sanskrit: alaṃ trāsena sugrīva bāṣpavego nigṛhyatām evaṃ prāyāṇi yuddhāni vijayo nāsti naiṣṭhikaḥ
english: "Enough of fear, Sugrīva; restrain the surge of tears. Such is the nature of battles — victory is not final for anyone."

sanskrit: saśeṣabhāgyatāsmākaṃ yadi vīra bhaviṣyati moham etau prahāsyete bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "If, O hero, some portion of our fortune still remains, these two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa will shake off their swoon."

sanskrit: paryavasthāpayātmānam anāthaṃ māṃ ca vānara satyadharmānuraktānāṃ nāsti mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam
english: "Steady yourself, O monkey, and steady me who am without a protector. For those devoted to truth and dharma there is no fear wrought by death."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tatas tasya jalaklinnena pāṇinā sugrīvasya śubhe netre pramamārja vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Vibhīṣaṇa then wiped Sugrīva's beautiful eyes with his hand, wet with water.

sanskrit: pramṛjya vadanaṃ tasya kapirājasya dhīmataḥ abravīt kālasaṃprātam asaṃbhrāntam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having wiped the face of that wise king of monkeys, he spoke these words, measured to the occasion and unperturbed.

sanskrit: na kālaḥ kapirājendra vaiklavyam anuvartitum atisneho 'py akāle 'smin maraṇāyopapadyate
english: "This is not the time, O king of monkeys, to give way to despondency. Even excessive love, at such an inopportune moment, conduces to death."

sanskrit: tasmād utsṛjya vaiklavyaṃ sarvakāryavināśanam hitaṃ rāmapurogāṇāṃ sainyānām anucintyatām
english: "Therefore, abandoning despondency — destroyer of every effort — let us consider what is beneficial for the armies led by Rāma."

sanskrit: atha vā rakṣyatāṃ rāmo yāvat saṃjñā viparyayaḥ labdhasaṃjñau tu kākutsthau bhayaṃ no vyapaneṣyataḥ
english: "Or else, let Rāma be guarded until consciousness is lost no more; when the two Kākutsthas regain their senses, they will drive away our fear."

sanskrit: naitat kiṃ cana rāmasya na ca rāmo mumūrṣati na hy enaṃ hāsyate lakṣmīr durlabhā yā gatāyuṣām
english: "This is nothing at all for Rāma; nor does Rāma wish to die. For the Fortune that abandons those whose life is spent will not abandon him."

sanskrit: tasmād āśvāsayātmānaṃ balaṃ cāśvāsaya svakam yāvat sarvāṇi sainyāni punaḥ saṃsthāpayāmy aham
english: "Therefore, comfort yourself and comfort your own forces, while I reassemble all the armies."

sanskrit: ete hy utphullanayanās trāsād āgatasādhvasāḥ karṇe karṇe prakathitā harayo haripuṃgava
english: "These monkeys, O bull among monkeys, eyes dilated wide, seized with dread and fear, are whispering in each other's ears."

sanskrit: māṃ tu dṛṣṭvā pradhāvantam anīkaṃ saṃpraharṣitum tyajantu harayas trāsaṃ bhuktapūrvām iva srajam
english: "Seeing me run forward to hearten the troops, let the monkeys abandon their fear as one discards a garland already worn."

sanskrit: samāśvāsya tu sugrīvaṃ rākṣasendro vibhīṣaṇaḥ vidrutaṃ vānarānīkaṃ tat samāśvāsayat punaḥ
english: Having heartened Sugrīva, the lord of rākṣasas Vibhīṣaṇa then heartened once more the scattered monkey army.

sanskrit: indrajit tu mahāmāyaḥ sarvasainyasamāvṛtaḥ viveśa nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ pitaraṃ cābhyupāgamat
english: Meanwhile Indrajit, master of great illusion, surrounded by all his forces, entered the city of Laṅkā and approached his father.

sanskrit: tatra rāvaṇam āsīnam abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ ācacakṣe priyaṃ pitre nihatau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: There, saluting the seated Rāvaṇa with joined palms, he reported the joyful news to his father: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa had been slain.

sanskrit: utpapāta tato hṛṣṭaḥ putraṃ ca pariṣasvaje rāvaṇo rakṣasāṃ madhye śrutvā śatrū nipātitau
english: Rāvaṇa then leapt up with joy and embraced his son, in the midst of the rākṣasas, having heard that the two enemies had been laid low.

sanskrit: upāghrāya sa mūrdhny enaṃ papraccha prītamānasaḥ pṛcchate ca yathāvṛttaṃ pitre sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: Smelling him on the head with affection and a gladdened heart, he questioned him; and to his father who questioned him, Indrajit reported everything just as it had occurred.

sanskrit: sa harṣavegānugatāntarātmā śrutvā vacas tasya mahārathasya jahau jvaraṃ dāśaratheḥ samutthitaṃ prahṛṣya vācābhinananda putram
english: His inner heart carried away by the surge of joy, having heard the words of that great warrior, Rāvaṇa shed the fever that had arisen on account of Daśaratha's son; and rejoicing, he praised his son with words.
